title: Abraham Wald concluded the most damaged planes don't return; per Vintage Aviation News, the army began increasing armor on vulnerable areas

trailer.text: According to the Deutsche Biographie, Abraham Wald was a Jewish mathematician and statistician, born in Cluj in 1902.
According to the Dictionary of Scientific Biography, after Hitler occupied Austria in 1938, Wald moved to the United States, and so was saved from death in a concentration camp.
According to MacTutor, during World War II he worked in the statistical group at Columbia and developed a method for estimating the vulnerability of aircraft.
In the famous story, as told by Bill Casselman, Wald said that the planes that were hit the most do not return, and therefore are not seen.
According to Vintage Aviation News, the military accepted his advice and began increasing the armor on the more vulnerable areas of the aircraft.

stations.title: A boy from Cluj who studied at home

paragraphs.text: According to the Deutsche Biographie, Wald was born on October 31, 1902, in Cluj.
According to MacTutor, he was born into a Jewish family of intellectuals, which was forced to earn its living in trades far from its abilities because it was Jewish.
According to Casselman, his mother tongue was Hungarian.
According to MacTutor, he did not attend primary or secondary school, but was educated at home by members of his family.
According to the Deutsche Biographie, he completed his studies in Cluj and moved to Vienna.
According to MacTutor, in the Vienna of the 1930s there was no place in an academic position for a young Jewish man, even if he was talented.
According to Casselman, Wald, as a Jew, was lucky to be able to move to the United States, like others in his situation.
According to MacTutor, in 1938 the Nazi forces invaded Austria, and for a Jewish person like Wald conditions under the Nazis were at best extremely difficult and at worst very dangerous.
According to MacTutor, the move to the United States almost certainly saved his life.
According to the Deutsche Biographie, his parents, his sisters and his brother Martin were murdered in the Holocaust, and only his brother Herman survived.

stations.title: 1943: The bombers that did not return

paragraphs.text: According to Outlook India, in 1943 the British Royal Air Force carried out massive bombing raids on Germany every night.
According to the same source, there were no long-range fighters, so the heavy bombers flew without escort.
According to Outlook India, many bombers were shot down by anti-aircraft fire from the ground or by Luftwaffe fighters.
In the popular version cited by Casselman, in 1943 American bombers suffered badly from German air defense, and the military sought advice on how to cut losses.
According to War History Online, after many American aircraft were lost, the military wanted to increase the armor of its bombers so that they would survive.

stations.title: A room of statisticians at Columbia

paragraphs.text: According to Casselman, the Statistical Research Group (SRG) was one of several groups of scientists formed soon after America entered the war.
According to Vintage Aviation News, the group was based at Columbia University, and it was the one that received the project to reduce losses.
According to Casselman, its beginnings in the summer of 1942 are told well in the memoir of W. Allen Wallis.

According to Casselman, those serving in the group included many of the most prominent statisticians of the post-war world, as well as the economists Milton Friedman and George Stigler, who later won the Nobel Prize in Economics, and the mathematician Abraham Wald.
According to War History Online, Wallis, the group's director, described it as the most extraordinary group of statisticians ever organized.
According to the same site, the group was given the task of analyzing the damage suffered by Allied aircraft from enemy fire and recommending how to increase their chances of survival.
According to Vintage Aviation News, technically Wald was not authorized to work on the projects in which he took part.

According to We Are The Mighty, drawing on Jordan Ellenberg, there was a running joke in the group that his secretaries had to tear the pages he had written out of his hands, because he did not have clearance to read his own work.
According to Casselman, Wald was given data on the number of planes sent out on missions, the number of planes that returned, and the number of hits on each plane that returned.
According to War History Online, the bullet holes in the returning bombers were concentrated on the wings and fuselage, almost twice as much as in areas such as the engines.
According to Outlook India, Wald's rough sketches showed that the wings, nose and fuselage took the most hits.
Wallis wrote, according to Casselman, that the military was inclined to protect the parts that showed the most hits on the returning planes.
According to We Are The Mighty, Wald found that the Navy wanted to armor the least vulnerable parts of the plane.
According to Casselman, Wald's first simplifying assumption was that planes were downed because of enemy fire.
Wallis wrote, according to Casselman, that Wald assumed, on good evidence, that hits in combat were uniformly distributed over the planes.
According to Outlook India, Wald assumed that the damage was random, that is, that the German anti-aircraft gunners and pilots did not aim at particular areas.

stations.title: The insight: look for what did not return

paragraphs.text: In the popular version quoted by Casselman, Wald says that the planes that are most damaged do not return, and therefore are not seen.
In the same version, Wald states that armor should be added around the engines.
According to War History Online, he concluded that armor should be placed on the areas that seemingly received the least damage.
According to Outlook India, he recommended armoring the cockpit, the engines and the tail.
According to Outlook India, Wald calculated that the highest chance of an aircraft being destroyed by a single hit was when a cannon shell hit an engine, followed by a hit to the cockpit.

According to a caption on the Vintage Aviation News website, based partly on a 1943 report by Wald, a similar plane survived a single hit to the engine in about 60% of cases, and a hit to the fuselage or fuel system in about 95%.
According to We Are The Mighty, Wald did not directly say to armor the opposite areas, but developed a highly technical method to estimate where the planes that did not return had been hit.
According to Vintage Aviation News, the military accepted Wald's advice and began increasing the armor on the more vulnerable areas of the aircraft.
According to We Are The Mighty, after the military added armor according to Wald's work, planes began surviving more hits.
According to We Are The Mighty, Wald convinced the Navy that it was about to armor the wrong parts of its planes, and so saved hundreds of flight crews.
According to War History Online, his work on survivorship bias helped improve the protection of bombers in World War II.
According to Vintage Aviation News, Wald's work was used to benefit aircraft also in Korea and Vietnam.
According to Outlook India, his methods still worked in Vietnam in the 1960s, when designers found that the F-4 Phantom rarely returned if its tail was damaged.

stations.title: After the war: a scientist, a family and an accident

paragraphs.text: According to MacTutor, Wald invented the field of sequential analysis when there was demand for more efficient methods of industrial quality control during the war.
According to the Dictionary of Scientific Biography, the two most important fields he founded are sequential analysis and the theory of decision functions.
According to the Deutsche Biographie, at Columbia he became assistant professor in 1942, associate professor in 1944 and full professor in 1945.
According to the same source, in 1948 he was president of the Institute of Mathematical Statistics and vice president of the American Statistical Association.
According to MacTutor, in the United States Wald met Lucille Lang and married her.
According to Vintage Aviation News, one of Wald's two children is Robert Wald, today a noted physicist.
According to Outlook India, in 1950 Wald traveled to India as a guest of the Indian government, which had invited him to lecture.
According to Vintage Aviation News, he and his wife were killed in a plane crash in the Nilgiri Mountains in southern India on December 13, 1950.
According to Casselman, Wald did not have the chance to write an autobiography.
According to Vintage Aviation News, his work was first published in a series of memoranda, and the Center for Naval Analyses reprinted it.

stations.title: How much of the story was actually documented

paragraphs.text: According to Bill Casselman, who wrote about the legend of Abraham Wald on the website of the American Mathematical Society (AMS), the famous story has a germ of truth, but very little evidence for the best bits.
According to Casselman, the source material on what Wald said about aircraft damage is especially scant.
According to Casselman, there are only two short and vague mentions of it in Wallis, and the collection of memoranda that Wald wrote.
According to Casselman, there are eight items among the memoranda, and five of them deal with estimating the probability of survival of a plane that has already been hit.
According to Casselman, the memoranda say nothing about what the military should do to improve the situation.
According to Casselman, Wallis's memoir focuses on Wald's work in the group on the invention of sequential analysis.
According to Vintage Aviation News, after his death Wald was criticized by many scholars, foremost among them Ronald Fisher, who attacked him as a mathematician without direct scientific experience.

claims.text: לפי Outlook India, וולד חישב שהסיכוי הגבוה ביותר להשמדת מטוס בפגיעה בודדת הוא פגיעת פגז תותח במנוע, ואחריה פגיעה בתא הטייס.
claims.quote: Wald specifically calculated that the highest chance of a single hit destroying an aircraft would be a cannon-shell hitting an engine, followed in terms of danger by a hit to the cockpit.

claims.text: לפי כיתוב באתר Vintage Aviation News, המבוסס באופן חלקי על דוח של וולד מ-1943, מטוס דומה שרד פגיעה בודדת במנוע כ-60% מהמקרים ופגיעה בגוף או במערכת הדלק כ-95%.
claims.quote: showing that a similar plane survived a single hit to the engine 60% of the time, but a hit to the fuselage or fuel system closer to 95% of the time

claims.text: לפי We Are The Mighty, לאחר שהצבא שריין לפי עבודתו של וולד, מטוסים החלו לשרוד יותר פגיעות.
claims.quote: instead of putting armor on the areas with the most observed hits. And guess what? Planes started surviving more hits.

claims.text: לפי We Are The Mighty, וולד שכנע את הצי שהוא עומד לשריין את החלקים הלא נכונים במטוסיו, וכך הציל מאות צוותי טיסה.
claims.quote: Wald convinced the Navy that it was about to armor the completely wrong parts of its planes, saving hundreds of flight crews in the process.

claims.text: לפי War History Online, עבודתו של וולד על הטיית שורדים סייעה לשפר את הגנת המפציצים במלחמת העולם השנייה.
claims.quote: One of his most notable successes was his work on survivorship bias, which helped improve bomber aircraft protection during WWII

claims.text: לפי Outlook India, שיטותיו של וולד עדיין עבדו בווייטנאם בשנות ה-60, כשמעצבים גילו שה-F-4 פאנטום כמעט לא חזר אם הזנב ניזוק.
claims.quote: Wald's methods still worked in Vietnam in the 1960s when aircraft designers noted that the US F-4 Phantom rarely returned if the tail was damaged.

claims.text: לפי MacTutor, וולד המציא את תחום הניתוח הסדרתי בתגובה לביקוש לשיטות יעילות יותר לבקרת איכות תעשייתית במלחמת העולם השנייה.
claims.quote: He invented the topic of sequential analysis in response to the demand for more efficient methods of industrial quality control during World War II.

claims.text: לפי המילון הביוגרפי למדעים, שני תחומי עבודתו החשובים ביותר של וולד, שהוא ייסד, הם הניתוח הסדרתי ותורת פונקציות ההחלטה.
claims.quote: we shall single out the two most important fields of his work, which he founded and in which his results still dominate: sequential analysis and the theory of decision functions

claims.text: לפי ה-Deutsche Biographie, בקולומביה הפך וולד ב-1942 לפרופסור עוזר, ב-1944 לפרופסור חבר וב-1945 לפרופסור מן המניין.
claims.quote: 1942 wurde er dort Assistant Professor, 1944 Associate Professor und 1945 Full Professor.

claims.text: לפי MacTutor, לאחר שהגר לארצות הברית פגש וולד את לוסיל לאנג ונישא לה.
claims.quote: After Wald emigrated to the United States he met Lucille Lang and the two were married.

claims.text: לפי Vintage Aviation News, אחד משני ילדי וולד הוא רוברט וולד, פיזיקאי מוכר כיום.
claims.quote: One of the children was Robert Wald, who is today a noted physicist.

claims.text: לפי Outlook India, וולד ואשתו מתו בהתרסקות מטוס בנילגירי ב-1950 כאשר נסע כאורח ממשלת הודו שהזמינה אותו להרצות.
claims.quote: He was travelling as a guest of the Indian government, which had invited him to deliver a series of lectures.

claims.text: לפי Vintage Aviation News, וולד ואשתו נהרגו בהתרסקות מטוס בהרי הנילגירי בדרום הודו ב-13 בדצמבר 1950.
claims.quote: Wald and his wife were killed in a plane crash near the Rangaswamy Pillar in the northern part of the Nilgiri Mountains in southern India on December 13, 1950.

claims.text: לפי קסלמן, וולד מת בתאונת מטוס בהרים בדרום הודו ב-1950 ולא הספיק לכתוב אוטוביוגרפיה.
claims.quote: he died in an airplane accident in the mountains of southern India in 1950, and had no chance to write his autobiography.

claims.text: לפי Vintage Aviation News, עבודתו של וולד פורסמה תחילה בסדרת תזכירי SRC והודפסה מחדש על ידי המרכז לניתוחי ים.
claims.quote: His work was initially published in a series of SRC memoranda and reissued by the Center for Naval Analyses.

claims.text: לפי ביל קסלמן (AMS, 2016), יש בסיפור המפורסם גרעין אמת איתן, אך יש מעט מאוד ראיות לחלקיו הטובים ביותר.
claims.quote: The story might well be true, and there is certainly, as we shall see, a solid germ of truth in it, but there is very little evidence for the best bits.

claims.text: לפי קסלמן, חומר המקור על מה שוולד אמר על נזקי מטוסים דל במיוחד.
claims.quote: There is extremely little source material for what Wald had to say about aircraft damage.

claims.text: לפי קסלמן, על עבודת וולד בנושא נזקי מטוסים קיימים רק שני אזכורים קצרים ועמומים אצל וואליס ואוסף התזכירים שוולד כתב.
claims.quote: two short and rather vague mentions in Wallis' memoir of work on aircraft vulnerability and (2) the collection of the actual memoranda that Wald wrote on the subject

claims.text: לפי קסלמן, בין התזכירים שמונה פריטים, וחמישה מהם עוסקים בהערכת הסתברות ההישרדות של מטוס שכבר נפגע.
claims.quote: There are eight items among the memoranda. Five of them deal with a single problem, estimating probabilities of an airplane's survival, given that it has already been hit.

claims.text: לפי קסלמן, בתזכירים של וולד אין דבר על מה שהצבא צריך לעשות כדי לשפר את המצב.
claims.quote: In particular, Wald says nothing about what the military should do to improve things.

claims.text: לפי קסלמן, זיכרונות וואליס מתמקדים בעבודת וולד ב-SRG בהמצאת הניתוח הסדרתי (sequential analysis).
claims.quote: its coverage of Wald's work at the SRG concentrates on the invention of sequential analysis

claims.text: לפי Vintage Aviation News, לאחר מותו ביקרו חוקרים רבים את וולד, ובראשם רונלד פישר שתקף אותו כמתמטיקאי חסר ניסיון מדעי ישיר.
claims.quote: After his death, Wald was widely criticized by several scholars, most notably Sir Ronald A. Fisher, who attacked him for being a mathematician lacking direct scientific experience.

claims.text: לפי פיל דפוי, שקיבל את החומרים מוואליס, הוא פרסם שמונה 'מאמרים' תחת שמו של וולד ביולי 1980.
claims.quote: With some minimal editing, I published eight 'papers' under Wald's name in July 1980.

claims.text: לפי War History Online, וולד סיים לימודי מתמטיקה באוניברסיטת קלוז' ב-1928.
claims.quote: He graduated in mathematics from King Ferdinand I University in 1928, and graduated from the University of Vienna with a Ph.D. in mathematics in 1931.

claims.text: לפי War History Online, אין נתונים על כמה חיים הציל הדבר במלחמה או אחריה.
claims.quote: Statistics on how many lives this saved during the war or since then are unavailable
